The value of sec 60° · cos 30° is

text: If tan 3A = √3, where 3A is an acute angle, then A equals
answer: Correct option: C) 20°. tan 60° = √3, so 3A = 60° and A = 20°.

text: If sin θ − cos θ = 1/2, then the value of sin θ cos θ is
answer: Correct option: A) 3/8. Squaring: sin²θ + cos²θ − 2 sin θ cos θ = 1/4, so 1 − 2 sin θ cos θ = 1/4, giving sin θ cos θ = (3/4)/2 = 3/8.

text: The value of (1 + tan²θ)(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ) is
answer: Correct option: D) 1. (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ) = 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ and 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, so the product is sec²θ · cos²θ = 1.

text: If 7 sin²θ + 3 cos²θ = 4 and θ is acute, then tan θ equals
answer: Correct option: B) 1/√3. 7 sin²θ + 3(1 − sin²θ) = 4 gives 4 sin²θ = 1, so sin θ = 1/2, θ = 30° and tan 30° = 1/√3.

text: If sec θ = 13/12, then (2 sin θ − 3 cos θ)/(4 sin θ − 9 cos θ) equals
answer: Correct option: C) 13/44. cos θ = 12/13 and sin θ = 5/13. Numerator = 10/13 − 36/13 = −26/13; denominator = 20/13 − 108/13 = −88/13. Ratio = 26/88 = 13/44.

text: If cosec A = 17/8 and A is acute, then tan A equals
answer: Correct option: C) 8/15. sin A = 8/17, so with hypotenuse 17 and perpendicular 8 the base is √(289 − 64) = 15. Hence tan A = 8/15.

text: sec θ (1 − sin θ)(sec θ + tan θ) is equal to
answer: Correct option: B) 1. sec θ + tan θ = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ, so the expression = (1/cos θ)(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)/cos θ = (1 − sin²θ)/cos²θ = 1.

text: sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ is equal to
answer: Correct option: B) 2 sin²θ − 1. sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) = 2 sin²θ − 1.

text: tan²θ − sin²θ is equal to
answer: Correct option: D) tan²θ sin²θ. tan²θ − sin²θ = tan²θ − tan²θ cos²θ = tan²θ(1 − cos²θ) = tan²θ sin²θ.

text: 1/(1 + sin A) + 1/(1 − sin A) is equal to
answer: Correct option: B) 2 sec²A. Sum = (1 − sin A + 1 + sin A)/(1 − sin²A) = 2/cos²A = 2 sec²A.

text: (1 + tan²A)/(1 + cot²A) is equal to
answer: Correct option: C) tan²A. 1 + tan²A = sec²A and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A, so the ratio = sin²A/cos²A = tan²A.

text: If x = sec θ + tan θ, then sec θ − tan θ is equal to
answer: Correct option: C) 1/x. (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, so sec θ − tan θ = 1/x.

text: cos θ/(1 − sin θ) is equal to
answer: Correct option: C) sec θ + tan θ. Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin θ): cos θ(1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin²θ) = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ = sec θ + tan θ.

text: (sin θ + cosec θ)² + (cos θ + sec θ)² is equal to
answer: Correct option: D) 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ. Expanding: sin²θ + 2 + cosec²θ + cos²θ + 2 + sec²θ = 1 + 4 + (1 + cot²θ) + (1 + tan²θ) = 7 + tan²θ + cot²θ.

text: A kite string, 40 m long, is held taut and makes an angle of 60° with the level ground. Ignoring any sag and taking the hand at ground level, the height of the kite above the ground is
answer: Correct option: B) 20√3 m. Height = 40 sin 60° = 40 × √3/2 = 20√3 m.

text: A ladder reaches a window 9 m above the ground and makes an angle of 30° with the ground. The length of the ladder is
answer: Correct option: C) 18 m. sin 30° = 9/L, so L = 9/(1/2) = 18 m.

text: An observer on the roof of a 20 m high building sees a car on level ground at an angle of depression of 30°. The distance of the car from the foot of the building is
answer: Correct option: D) 20√3 m. The angle of elevation of the roof from the car is also 30°, so tan 30° = 20/d, giving d = 20√3 m.

text: From a point on level ground the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 45°. After walking 30 m towards the foot of the tower the angle of elevation becomes 60°. The height of the tower is
answer: Correct option: B) 15(3 + √3) m. Let height h. Distances from foot: h/tan 45° = h and h/tan 60° = h/√3. So h − h/√3 = 30, h = 30√3/(√3 − 1) = 15√3(√3 + 1) = 15(3 + √3) m.

text: A vertical pole 12 m high casts a shadow 4√3 m long on level ground. The angle of elevation of the Sun is
answer: Correct option: C) 60°. tan θ = 12/(4√3) = 3/√3 = √3, so θ = 60°.

text: From the top of a 60 m high cliff, the angles of depression of two boats on the same side, in line with the foot of the cliff, are 30° and 60°. The distance between the boats is
answer: Correct option: B) 40√3 m. Distances from the foot: 60/tan 30° = 60√3 and 60/tan 60° = 20√3. Difference = 40√3 m.

text:
Assertion (A): (1 + tan²θ) cos²θ = 1 for every acute angle θ.
Reason (R): 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. R is the standard identity; using it, (1 + tan²θ) cos²θ = sec²θ cos²θ = 1, so A follows directly from R.

text:
Assertion (A): There is an acute angle θ for which sec θ = 3/5.
Reason (R): In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is the longest side, so sec θ = hypotenuse/base is always greater than 1 for an acute angle θ.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: D) A is false but R is true. R is true. Since sec θ > 1 for every acute angle, sec θ = 3/5 < 1 is impossible, so A is false.

text: Evaluate: 4 sin²30° + 3 tan²60° − 2 sec²45°.
If sin (A + B) = 1 and cos (A − B) = √3/2, where 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find the values of A and B.
answer:
sin (A + B) = 1 = sin 90°, so A + B = 90°.
cos (A − B) = √3/2 = cos 30°, so A − B = 30°.
Adding: 2A = 120°, A = 60°; then B = 30°.
Answer: A = 60°, B = 30°

text: If sin θ + cos θ = 5/4, find the value of sin θ cos θ and hence of tan θ + cot θ.
answer:
Squaring: 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ = 25/16, so 2 sin θ cos θ = 9/16 and sin θ cos θ = 9/32.
tan θ + cot θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(9/32) = 32/9.
Answer: sin θ cos θ = 9/32; tan θ + cot θ = 32/9

text: Find the value of p if p sin 30° + 4 cos²60° = 3 tan²45° + cosec 30°.
If 13 sin A = 5 and A is acute, evaluate (5 sin A − 2 cos A)/tan A.
Prove that cos θ/(1 + sin θ) + (1 + sin θ)/cos θ = 2 sec θ.
answer:
LHS = [cos²θ + (1 + sin θ)²]/[cos θ (1 + sin θ)]
= [cos²θ + 1 + 2 sin θ + sin²θ]/[cos θ (1 + sin θ)]
= [2 + 2 sin θ]/[cos θ (1 + sin θ)] = 2(1 + sin θ)/[cos θ (1 + sin θ)] = 2/cos θ = 2 sec θ = RHS. Hence proved.

text: Prove that sin θ (1 + tan θ) + cos θ (1 + cot θ) = sec θ + cosec θ.
answer:
LHS = sin θ + sin²θ/cos θ + cos θ + cos²θ/sin θ
= (sin θ + cos²θ/sin θ) + (cos θ + sin²θ/cos θ)
= (sin²θ + cos²θ)/sin θ + (cos²θ + sin²θ)/cos θ
= 1/sin θ + 1/cos θ = cosec θ + sec θ = RHS. Hence proved.

text: A vertical tower casts a shadow 15 m long on level ground when the angle of elevation of the Sun is 60°. Find the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
Let height = h. tan 60° = h/15, so h = 15√3 = 15 × 1.73 = 25.95 m.
Answer: 25.95 m

text: From a point on level ground 30 m from the foot of a vertical pole, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 30°. Find the height of the pole and the distance of the top of the pole from the point. (Leave answers in surd form.)
answer:
tan 30° = h/30, so h = 30/√3 = 10√3 m.
Distance of top = √(30² + (10√3)²) = √(900 + 300) = √1200 = 20√3 m (also 30/cos 30° = 20√3).
Answer: height 10√3 m; distance 20√3 m

text: A boy 1.5 m tall stands 20 m away from a vertical pole. The angle of elevation of the top of the pole from his eyes (take eye level as 1.5 m above ground) is 45°. Find the height of the pole above the ground.
answer:
Height of the pole above his eye level = 20 tan 45° = 20 m.
Total height = 20 + 1.5 = 21.5 m.
Answer: 21.5 m

text: Prove that (cot θ − cos θ)/(cot θ + cos θ) = (cosec θ − 1)/(cosec θ + 1).
answer:
LHS = (cos θ/sin θ − cos θ)/(cos θ/sin θ + cos θ) = cos θ(1/sin θ − 1)/[cos θ(1/sin θ + 1)]
= (cosec θ − 1)/(cosec θ + 1) = RHS. Hence proved.

text: Prove that (sec θ − cos θ)/(sec θ + cos θ) = sin²θ/(1 + cos²θ).
answer: LHS = (1/cos θ − cos θ)/(1/cos θ + cos θ) = [(1 − cos²θ)/cos θ]/[(1 + cos²θ)/cos θ] = (1 − cos²θ)/(1 + cos²θ) = sin²θ/(1 + cos²θ) = RHS. Hence proved.

text: Prove that (1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)².
answer: RHS = (1/cos θ + sin θ/cos θ)² = (1 + sin θ)²/cos²θ = (1 + sin θ)²/(1 − sin²θ) = (1 + sin θ)²/[(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)] = (1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ) = LHS. Hence proved.

text: Prove that tan²θ/(1 + tan²θ) + cot²θ/(1 + cot²θ) = 1.
answer:
tan²θ/(1 + tan²θ) = tan²θ/sec²θ = (sin²θ/cos²θ) × cos²θ = sin²θ.
cot²θ/(1 + cot²θ) = cot²θ/cosec²θ = (cos²θ/sin²θ) × sin²θ = cos²θ.
Sum = sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 = RHS. Hence proved.

text: Prove that (cosec θ − sin θ)(sec θ − cos θ)(tan θ + cot θ) = 1.
answer:
cosec θ − sin θ = (1 − sin²θ)/sin θ = cos²θ/sin θ.
sec θ − cos θ = (1 − cos²θ)/cos θ = sin²θ/cos θ.
tan θ + cot θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ).
Product = (cos²θ/sin θ)(sin²θ/cos θ)(1/(sin θ cos θ)) = (sin θ cos θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1. Hence proved.

text: If tan θ + sin θ = m and tan θ − sin θ = n, prove that m² − n² = 4√(mn).
answer:
m² − n² = (m + n)(m − n) = (2 tan θ)(2 sin θ) = 4 tan θ sin θ.
mn = tan²θ − sin²θ = sin²θ(1/cos²θ − 1) = sin²θ tan²θ.
So √(mn) = tan θ sin θ (for acute θ) and 4√(mn) = 4 tan θ sin θ = m² − n². Hence proved.

text: A flagstaff 10 m high stands on top of a tower. From a point on level ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and the top of the flagstaff are 30° and 45° respectively. Find the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
Let tower height = h and distance of the point from its foot = d.
Bottom of flagstaff (top of tower): tan 30° = h/d, so d = h√3.
Top of flagstaff: tan 45° = (h + 10)/d = 1, so d = h + 10.
h√3 = h + 10, so h(√3 − 1) = 10, h = 10/(√3 − 1) = 5(√3 + 1) = 5 × 2.73 = 13.65 m.
Answer: 13.65 m

text: Two points A and B lie on level ground on opposite sides of a 30 m high tower and in line with its foot. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from A and B are 30° and 60° respectively. Find the distance AB. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
Distance of A from foot = 30/tan 30° = 30√3 m. Distance of B from foot = 30/tan 60° = 10√3 m.
Since A and B are on opposite sides, AB = 30√3 + 10√3 = 40√3 = 40 × 1.73 = 69.2 m.
Answer: 69.2 m

text: Evaluate: (sin 35°/cos 55°)² + tan 20° tan 70° + 3 sec 25° sin 65° − 2 tan 17° tan 73°.
answer:
Using sin (90° − x) = cos x etc.: sin 35° = cos 55°, so the first term is 1² = 1.
tan 70° = cot 20°, so tan 20° tan 70° = 1.
sin 65° = cos 25°, so sec 25° sin 65° = 1 and the third term is 3.
tan 73° = cot 17°, so tan 17° tan 73° = 1 and the last term is 2.
Value = 1 + 1 + 3 − 2 = 3.
Answer: 3

text: If 15 cot A = 8 and A is acute, find sin A, sec A and the value of (1 + sin A)/(1 − sin A).
answer:
cot A = 8/15: base 8, perpendicular 15, hypotenuse = √(64 + 225) = 17.
sin A = 15/17, sec A = 17/8.
(1 + sin A)/(1 − sin A) = (32/17)/(2/17) = 16.
Answer: sin A = 15/17, sec A = 17/8, expression = 16

text: A tower stands on top of a 20 m high building. From a point P on level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the building is 45° and that of the top of the tower is 60°. Find (i) the distance of P from the foot of the building and (ii) the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
(i) tan 45° = 20/d, so d = 20 m.
(ii) Let the tower height be x; its top is at height 20 + x. tan 60° = (20 + x)/20, so 20 + x = 20√3 and x = 20(√3 − 1) = 20 × 0.73 = 14.6 m.
Answer: 20 m; 14.6 m

text: A boat approaches the foot of a 90 m high lighthouse in a straight line. A keeper at the top first sees the boat at an angle of depression of 30°; 6 minutes later the angle of depression is 60°. Assuming the boat moves at constant speed, find (i) the distance the boat covered in the 6 minutes, (ii) its speed in metres per minute, and (iii) how much more time it will take to reach the foot of the lighthouse. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
Let initial distance from the foot be d1 and later distance d2.
d1 = 90/tan 30° = 90√3 m; d2 = 90/tan 60° = 30√3 m.
(i) Distance covered = 90√3 − 30√3 = 60√3 = 60 × 1.73 = 103.8 m.
(ii) Speed = 103.8/6 = 17.3 m per minute.
(iii) Remaining distance = 30√3 = 51.9 m; time = 51.9/17.3 = 3 minutes.
(Check: ratio 30√3 : 60√3 = 1 : 2, so remaining time is half of 6 minutes.)
Answer: 103.8 m; 17.3 m/min; 3 minutes

text: A point is 40 m above the surface of a lake. The angle of elevation of a cloud from this point is 45° and the angle of depression of the cloud's reflection in the lake, from the same point, is 60°. Find the height of the cloud above the lake. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
Let the cloud be H m above the lake and let the horizontal distance of the cloud from the point be d. The reflection is H m below the lake surface.
Cloud is (H − 40) m above the point: tan 45° = (H − 40)/d, so d = H − 40.
Reflection is (H + 40) m below the point: tan 60° = (H + 40)/d, so H + 40 = √3 d = √3 (H − 40).
H(√3 − 1) = 40(√3 + 1), H = 40(√3 + 1)/(√3 − 1) = 40(√3 + 1)²/2 = 20(4 + 2√3) = 40(2 + √3).
H = 40 × 3.73 = 149.2 m.
Answer: about 149.2 m

text: Standing on the roof of a 24 m high building, a surveyor observes the foot of a transmission tower at an angle of depression of 45° and its top at an angle of elevation of 30°. The tower and building are on level ground. Find (i) the horizontal distance between the building and the tower, and (ii) the height of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
(i) Angle of depression of the foot is 45°, so tan 45° = 24/d, giving d = 24 m.
(ii) The top of the tower is above roof level by y: tan 30° = y/24, so y = 24/√3 = 8√3 = 8 × 1.73 = 13.84 m.
Height of the tower = 24 + 13.84 = 37.84 m.
Answer: 24 m; 37.84 m

text: An aeroplane flies horizontally at a constant height of 900 m directly away from an observer on the ground. When first seen, its angle of elevation is 45°; after 20 seconds it is 30°. Find the distance flown in 20 seconds and the speed of the aeroplane in m/s and in km/h. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
Horizontal distances from the observer: d1 = 900/tan 45° = 900 m; d2 = 900/tan 30° = 900√3 m.
Distance flown = 900√3 − 900 = 900(0.73) = 657 m.
Speed = 657/20 = 32.85 m/s.
In km/h: 32.85 × 18/5 = 118.26 km/h.
Answer: 657 m; 32.85 m/s (118.26 km/h)

text: The angle of elevation of the top of a vertical tower from a point A on level ground is 60°. From a point B on a vertical pole, 20 m above A, in the same vertical plane as the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 45°. Find (i) the height of the tower and (ii) the horizontal distance of the tower from the pole. (Use √3 = 1.73)
answer:
Let tower height = h and horizontal distance = d.
From A: tan 60° = h/d, so h = d√3.
From B (20 m up): the top is (h − 20) above B, so tan 45° = (h − 20)/d, giving h − 20 = d.
d√3 − 20 = d, so d(√3 − 1) = 20, d = 20/(√3 − 1) = 10(√3 + 1) = 10 × 2.73 = 27.3 m.
h = d√3 = 10(3 + √3) = 10 × 4.73 = 47.3 m.
Answer: tower 47.3 m high; horizontal distance 27.3 m

text:
Kite flying. Aarav stands on level ground and flies a kite. The string is taut and straight, 100 m long, and makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal ground. Take Aarav's hand to be at ground level.
(i) Find the height of the kite above the ground. [1]
(ii) Find the horizontal distance between Aarav and the point on the ground directly below the kite. [1]
(iii) The kite stays at the same height. Aarav walks towards the point below it until the string makes 45° with the ground. Find the new length of the string. (Use √2 = 1.41) [2]
OR
(iii) Find how far Aarav walked in the situation above. (Use √3 = 1.73) [2]
answer:
(i) Height = 100 sin 30° = 50 m.
(ii) Horizontal distance = 100 cos 30° = 50√3 m (about 86.5 m).
(iii) Kite height is still 50 m. At 45°: string length = 50/sin 45° = 50√2 = 50 × 1.41 = 70.5 m.
OR (iii) At 45° the horizontal distance = 50/tan 45° = 50 m. Distance walked = 50√3 − 50 = 50(0.73) = 36.5 m.

text:
Apartment and the ground. A residential apartment block is 30 m high and stands on level ground. A point P on the ground, in line with the foot of the block, sees the top of the block at an angle of elevation of 60°.
(i) Find the distance of P from the foot of the block. [1]
(ii) What is the angle of depression of P as seen from the top of the block? Justify your answer. [1]
(iii) Rohan walks directly away from the block until the angle of elevation of the top becomes 30°. Find the distance he walked. (Use √3 = 1.73) [2]
OR
(iii) Find the length of the line of sight from Rohan to the top of the block when the angle of elevation is 30°. [2]
answer:
(i) tan 60° = 30/d, so d = 30/√3 = 10√3 m (about 17.3 m).
(ii) The line of sight from P to the top and the horizontal line through the top are parallel to the ground, so the angle of depression equals the angle of elevation (alternate angles): 60°.
(iii) At 30°: distance = 30/tan 30° = 30√3 m. Distance walked = 30√3 − 10√3 = 20√3 = 20 × 1.73 = 34.6 m.
OR (iii) Line of sight = 30/sin 30° = 60 m.

text:
The painter's ladder. A painter uses a 16 m long ladder to reach a wall. The ladder rests against a vertical wall on level ground and makes an angle of 60° with the ground.
(i) How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall? [1]
(ii) How high up the wall does the ladder reach? (Leave in surd form.) [1]
(iii) For safety the painter changes the position of the foot of the ladder so that the same ladder makes 45° with the ground. Find how much lower the top of the ladder now is on the wall. (Use √2 = 1.41, √3 = 1.73) [2]
OR
(iii) Find how much farther from the wall the foot of the ladder now is. (Use √2 = 1.41) [2]
answer:
(i) Distance = 16 cos 60° = 8 m.
(ii) Height = 16 sin 60° = 8√3 m.
(iii) New height = 16 sin 45° = 8√2 = 8 × 1.41 = 11.28 m. Original height = 8 × 1.73 = 13.84 m. The top is lower by 13.84 − 11.28 = 2.56 m.
OR (iii) New distance = 16 cos 45° = 8√2 = 11.28 m. The foot is farther by 11.28 − 8 = 3.28 m.

text:
Balloon festival. A hot-air balloon hovers 90 m above level ground at a point directly above a spot O. Two observers A and B stand on opposite sides of O, in line with it. From A the angle of elevation of the balloon is 30° and from B it is 60°.
(i) Find the distance OA. [1]
(ii) Find the distance OB. [1]
(iii) Observer A walks towards O until the angle of elevation of the balloon is 45°. Find the distance A walked and the new distance between A and B (B has not moved). (Use √3 = 1.73) [2]
answer:
(i) OA = 90/tan 30° = 90√3 m.
(ii) OB = 90/tan 60° = 30√3 m.
(iii) At 45° the new distance from O is 90/tan 45° = 90 m. Distance walked by A = 90√3 − 90 = 90(0.73) = 65.7 m.
New distance AB = 90 + 30√3 = 90 + 51.9 = 141.9 m (A and B are still on opposite sides of O).
